Subject: Re: Performance SLOs — proposed quotas and feasibility notes

Hi Sam / team — quick technical response after reviewing the call notes and the SLO template Marissa attached. TL;DR: this is achievable on Redwood with the right capacity profile; below are recommended quotas and behaviors for the POC. I attached an updated quote (concurrency-quote-v2.pdf) with Dedicated capacity pricing and burst options.

Technical feasibility and recommendations:
- Latency: p99 350–400ms for <=256 token completions is realistic on verified open models (and Redwood-verified profiles) when serving from Dedicated capacity with optimized kernels. For hosted tiers we can get close but may need higher headroom on concurrency.
- Concurrency model (recommended):
  • Global concurrency quota (soft): 1,500 concurrent requests
  • Sustained concurrency target: 400 concurrent requests (for steady-state billing)
  • Short-duration burst headroom: up to 3,500 concurrent requests for 10–30 minute windows (auto-burst with buffer)
- Token throughput:
  • Daily steady-state: 1.5–2.5M tokens/day supported easily on Dedicated SKU recommended for predictable latency
  • Peak token rate: configure for up to 200k tokens/minute during heavy batch periods
- Per-connection / client guidance:
  • HTTP/2 (recommended) or gRPC for multiplexing — target 60–100 persistent connections from your fleet per region
  • Use connection pooling and keep-alive; avoid creating new TLS handshakes per request
  • Recommend client-side request concurrency limit per connection = 8–16 (i.e., if you have 80 connections, this supports ~640–1,280 parallel inflight requests)
- Streaming: supported via chunked responses / SSE. For heavy streaming workloads keep chunk sizes modest (16–64 tokens) to reduce latency spikes and allow progressive rendering.
- Redwood rate limits & quotas (proposed for POC):
  • Request-level RPS soft limit: 5,000 RPS (configurable)
  • Concurrent request soft limit: 1,500 (as above)
  • Token ingestion rate soft limit: 250k tokens/second aggregate (configurable for Dedicated)
  • Hard limits will be negotiated on contract but we can provision higher ceilings for Dedicated reserved capacity

Operational notes:
- For lowest p99 latency we recommend pinning to a specific model version and using prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts.
- If you need strict SLA-backed latency we should move to Dedicated with reserved capacity and an SLA clause (included in the quote).

Next steps (suggested):
1) Marissa to send formal quote + PO template to procurement (I attached concurrency-quote-v2.pdf).
2) CloudOps to share detailed load curve (per-minute RPS + token size distribution) if you want tighter quota tuning.
3) Schedule a short tech call (30m) to walk client engineers through connection pooling and streaming best practices.

Happy to discuss further — I can also produce a sample client config with connection and concurrency knobs if that helps.

Cheers,
Michael Grant
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Performance SLOs — client connection guidance

Quick follow on from my side with client-level recommendations to hit the concurrency numbers Michael proposed:
- Use HTTP/2 or gRPC where possible to enable multiplexing; aim for 75–100 persistent connections per region.
- Set per-connection concurrency target to 10 inflight requests; with 80 connections that gives ~800 inflight requests. Scale connections up to reach desired concurrency, but monitor TCP sockets and NAT limits if running from a small number of hosts.
- Keep-alive + TLS session reuse is critical for latency. Configure 60s keep-alive and aggressive reuse on the client side.
- Backoff strategy: implement jittered exponential backoff for 429 responses; use the Retry-After header on rate limit responses.
- Telemetry: emit per-request timing and queue-depth metrics to help us tune batching and autoscale.

I can share a sample client config (env var names, concurrency knobs) in the tech call.

—Dev
